By the mid-2020s, its perception underwent a final evolution, transitioning from a digital assistant into the "central nervous system" of global infrastructure, capable of managing power grids, medical diagnoses, and complex industrial automation in real-time.
artificial-intelligence.facts: Artificial Intelligence is essentially "statistical intuition at scale"; by processing billions of parameters through layers of artificial neurons, it can identify subtle correlations in data that are completely invisible to the human mind. It acts as a cognitive accelerator when paired with quantum processors, as the quantum hardware handles the massive linear algebra calculations required for training at speeds thousands of times faster than silicon chips. Because AI models use "backpropagation," they learn from their own mistakes by calculating the error in their output and adjusting their internal weights to improve accuracy with every single iteration. Interestingly, a modern AI cluster can simulate millions of years of chemical reactions or physical stress tests in just a few days, allowing scientists to discover new life-saving drugs and ultra-strong materials without ever entering a physical laboratory.

hyperdrive-component.name: Hyperdrive Component
hyperdrive-component.description: A precision-engineered assembly designed to generate and sustain high-energy fields for the localized manipulation of spacetime metrics.
hyperdrive-component.historical_info: The hyperdrive component transitioned from a mathematical curiosity in the mid-20th century – stemming from solutions to Einstein's field equations – to the focus of modern breakthrough propulsion physics. Its value shifted from a localized trope in science fiction literature to a supreme strategic objective for international space agencies seeking to bypass the limitations of chemical rocketry. This transition moved the concept from the "warp drive" metrics proposed by Miguel Alcubierre in 1994 to laboratory-scale experiments involving vacuum fluctuations and dynamic Casimir effects. By the 21st century, its perception underwent an evolution, transitioning from a violation of causality into a rigorously studied theoretical framework that explores how negative energy densities might facilitate superluminal displacement without violating local relativity.
hyperdrive-component.facts: A hyperdrive component is essentially a "metric engineer"; it is designed to create a "warp bubble" that contracts space in front of a craft and expands it behind, allowing the vessel to be carried along like a surfer on a wave of spacetime. It acts as a "quantum stressor" by utilizing exotic matter or high-intensity electromagnetic fields to induce a negative energy density, a requirement for any propulsion system that seeks to exceed the speed of light. Because the energy requirements for such a device are astronomical, these components are often theorized to be powered by matter-antimatter annihilation or zero-point energy extraction. Interestingly, according to general relativity, while the ship inside the bubble never moves faster than light relative to its local surroundings, the bubble itself can move at any speed, potentially shortening a journey to Proxima Centauri from 6,000 years to just a few weeks.

hyperdrive-engine.name: Hyperdrive Engine
hyperdrive-engine.description: A transcendent propulsion architecture that integrates exotic matter reactors and quantum field stabilizers to facilitate superluminal interstellar transit.
hyperdrive-engine.historical_info: The hyperdrive engine transitioned from the imaginative "Faster-Than-Light" (FTL) concepts of the early 20th century to the most complex engineering challenge in human history. Its value shifted from a localized trope in speculative physics – rooted in the Alcubierre metric – to a supreme strategic necessity for the survival of the species. This transition moved the engine from theoretical "warp bubbles" and "wormholes" described in general relativity to a tangible hardware goal requiring the synthesis of every high-tier technology ever developed. By the modern era, its perception underwent a final evolution, transitioning from a mathematical impossibility into the ultimate technological milestone, representing the transition of humanity from a planetary society to a multi-stellar civilization.
hyperdrive-engine.facts: A hyperdrive engine is essentially a "space-time navigator"; it functions by generating a localized gravitational anomaly that permits a vessel to bypass the light-speed barrier without violating the laws of local causality. It acts as a "quantum-exotic bridge," where super-cooled quantum processors manage the stability of an exotic matter core to prevent the warp bubble from collapsing under immense gravitational stress. Because the system must calculate millions of spatial variables per microsecond to avoid stellar collisions, it requires an integrated Artificial Intelligence cluster to maintain the integrity of the flight path. Interestingly, while a hyperdrive engine enables travel across galaxies, the "ship" itself remains stationary within its own pocket of spacetime, meaning the crew experiences no G-force or time dilation, effectively allowing them to arrive at their destination younger than light itself would have been upon arrival.

director-orientation.title: Director Orientation
director-orientation.summary: Your assignment, the industrial loop, and what counts as progress.
director-orientation.unlockLabel: Available at the start of every assignment

sections.title: Your assignment
paragraphs: You are the acting Director of an industrial colony. Your practical job is to gather raw materials, turn them into increasingly sophisticated products, research new methods, construct the facilities those methods require, and join the resulting processes into long production chains.

There is no single permanently correct production line. Early resources remain relevant because advanced products often depend on several older branches at once. Treat every unlocked recipe as a reusable industrial capability, not as a rung you discard after climbing past it.
bullets: Gather or manufacture the resources required by an available research project.
Complete the research to unlock recipes, buildings, or a new branch of the technology tree.
Construct newly unlocked buildings; research alone does not make a building operational.
Produce the new intermediates, then repeat the cycle at a larger scale.
The long-term corporate objective is the Hyperdrive Engine. Reaching it requires the whole industrial network, not one isolated chain.

sections.title: There is no passive base production by default
paragraphs: Normal recipes execute when you press Produce. Inputs are consumed and outputs are delivered immediately. A building existing in your colony does not make it manufacture on its own. Continuous operation becomes possible only through automation schemes, and those schemes still need valid resources, program structure, and—where applicable—personnel or energy.

This makes planning more valuable than frantic clicking. Before committing a large batch, inspect all inputs, tool capacity, fuel, the maximum amount, and the next dependency you are trying to satisfy.

callout.title: Recommended first route
callout.body: Open either starting gathering site, collect Wood and Stone, then open Research. Basic Crafting is the first important junction: it introduces tools and expands your ability to gather efficiently.

sections.title: Progress is preserved, attention is not
paragraphs: Inventory, research, construction, statistics, unlocked records, operations-board items, automation programs, and Guide reading state are stored in the current save. Temporary interface state—such as an open modal or a half-entered search query—is not the same thing as saved industrial progress.

Corporate systems evaluate output with unusual enthusiasm. They do not require you to imitate that enthusiasm. Pausing to inspect the Almanac or redesign a program is part of running the colony correctly.

game-modes-and-training.title: Game Modes and Guided Training
game-modes-and-training.summary: The saved mode choice and the optional 32-step introduction to production, research, automation, planning, construction, the Almanac, and the Guide.
game-modes-and-training.unlockLabel: Available at the start of every assignment

sections.title: Choosing an assignment
paragraphs: A new game lets you choose an operating mode, difficulty, a save slot, and whether to run the guided training sequence. Hard starts with 0 colonists, Normal with 10, and Easy with 20; every new highest technology tier still adds 5. Easy also develops Operations Board projects instantly, while Normal and Hard retain the standard timer. Starting in an occupied slot asks for confirmation and then overwrites that slot. The Guide remains available in every mode and does not depend on training.

The selected mode is stored in the save as assignment metadata. In the current build, however, the simulation does not read that value after the new game is created: Standard and High-Realistic currently use the same recipes, costs, production rules, and failure conditions. The emissions and planetary-health rules described on the High-Realistic selection card are not active yet. Do not plan a current colony around an unimplemented pollution meter.
bullets: Standard: the honest default for the current ruleset.
High-Realistic: its choice is preserved in the slot, but it does not presently activate different mechanics. This Guide will describe those mechanics only after they exist in the simulation.
Guided training: a temporary 32-step voiced sequence led by Dr. Mira Holland. It can be skipped at any point and is not required to unlock Guide records.

Demo evaluation builds contain a bounded slice of the campaign and clearly identify their completion target. Full-game records should not be interpreted as a promise that unavailable demo content can be reached in that build.

sections.title: What guided training now covers
paragraphs: The current training has 32 steps. After the assignment briefing, it guides you through collecting batches of ten Wood and Stone, completing Basic Crafting research, and understanding the five-colonist capacity increase granted by a new highest research tier.

It then introduces Colonist Automation in the Tree Grove. You open the manual scheme editor, assemble and validate a continuous loop with a Production block set to ten iterations, start it, and use the Automation Board to inspect the running program.

The final practical sequence introduces project planning and construction: inspect Hand Crafting, pin its requirements, read the combined totals on the Operations Board, open the New Project planner to see how target projects later calculate long chains, gather anything still missing, and construct the building. Training then opens the Almanac and the Guide before the concluding briefing. It is a foundation tour, not a complete walkthrough of the campaign.

sections.title: How interactive steps behave
paragraphs: An interactive step highlights the relevant control and disables Next until the expected action is observed. Production steps verify both the selected recipe and the requested batch amount. The automation step verifies the required continuous manual scheme before allowing the sequence to continue. Completing an action advances automatically after a short delay.

The dialogue can be dragged during interactive steps and switched between compact and expanded layouts. Explanatory steps temporarily lock background scrolling, while action steps leave the required interface available. Clicking unrevealed dialogue finishes its typewriter animation immediately; it does not skip the required action. Skip closes the entire training sequence and stops its current voice line.

Training demonstrates a safe first route through the colony. The Guide explains the underlying rules and remains searchable afterward. Skipping training never removes mechanics, resources, or progression.

Guide records unlock when the relevant system enters your working context. A numbered badge on the Guide button shows how many available records you have not opened. Opening a record marks that record as read; it can always be revisited.

interface-and-navigation.title: Interface and Navigation
interface-and-navigation.summary: The command header, primary tabs, overlays, focus jumps, and back behavior.
interface-and-navigation.unlockLabel: Available at the start of every assignment

sections.title: The persistent command surface
paragraphs: The top of the game is divided into a status deck and a navigation strip. The central tabs—Buildings, Inventory, Research, and Almanac—change the main workspace. Achievements, Statistics, Guide, and Menu open as overlays above the current workspace, so closing them returns you to the same place.

Many links are contextual. Clicking a resource can open its exact Almanac page; clicking Open Research can focus the relevant technology node; an Operations Board action can jump to the required building or recipe. These jumps are deliberately preferable to manually searching a large late-game catalogue.

media.alt: The full game header with status cells, navigation tabs, Guide button, and notification badge.
media.caption: Primary command surface and overlay controls.

sections.title: Back, close, and modal priority
bullets: Escape closes the topmost supported overlay before changing the underlying screen.
Inside a production building, Back returns to the Buildings directory.
Pressing the Buildings tab while a production building is already open also returns to the directory.
From another main tab, Back returns to Buildings. From the Buildings directory, Back opens the game menu.
During a blocking cinematic, tutorial action, or later full-screen reveal, ordinary navigation may be intentionally suspended until that layer completes or is dismissed.

sections.title: Pinned and compact header behavior
paragraphs: Display settings can keep the complete header pinned while the main content scrolls, pin only a compact portion, remember the last Buildings-list position, and scale the UI. These are presentation settings; they do not alter production or unlocks.

callout.title: Small badges are live information
callout.body: Hotkey labels reflect your current bindings. The Guide badge reflects unlocked-but-unread records. Neither number is an achievement score.

keyboard-controls.title: Keyboard Controls
keyboard-controls.summary: Default shortcuts, contextual actions, rebinding, and intentional key sharing.
keyboard-controls.unlockLabel: Available at the start of every assignment

sections.title: Default global controls
bullets: Tab toggles the Operations Board.
A toggles the Automation Board.
Space runs the currently selected production recipe when production can proceed.
Enter confirms a highlighted action or opens a keyboard-selected item.
Escape performs Back / Close according to the current overlay stack.
Arrow keys move supported keyboard selections. F focuses the search field on screens that expose search.
F1 and F2 open Achievements and Statistics. F3–F6 select Buildings, Inventory, Research, and Almanac. F7 opens Menu.
Page Up and Page Down move to the top or bottom of the production interface. H hides or restores the production overlay so the facility artwork can be viewed.

sections.title: Production preset keys
paragraphs: Digits 1–6 select production presets (x10, x20, x50, x100, x1000, and MAX) while a production interface owns that context.
Duplicate bindings are rejected. If you rebind a command, the small labels shown on supported controls update to match. Hotkey hints themselves can be hidden without disabling the bindings.

sections.title: Rebinding safely
steps: Open Menu, then Settings, then Hotkeys.
Select the binding field for one action and press the desired key combination.
If the combination conflicts, choose another or reset the conflicting action first.
Use Reset on one row to restore one default, or Reset All Hotkeys to restore the complete map.

callout.title: Typing fields take priority
callout.body: Most global shortcuts are suppressed while you type into an input, search box, selector, or hotkey capture. Board toggles remain available by design. This prevents a search query from unexpectedly producing a batch or changing screens.

saving-and-slots.title: Saving, Slots, and Recovery
saving-and-slots.summary: Manual saves, autosaves, slot ownership, exports, backups, and what is persisted.
saving-and-slots.unlockLabel: Available at the start of every assignment

sections.title: Two save paths
paragraphs: Manual saves are written to the numbered slot you choose. Autosaves are written to a dedicated autosave record at the configured interval; they do not silently overwrite a numbered manual slot. Continue first uses the remembered manual slot and otherwise searches numbered slots from the beginning. Loading the autosave does not replace the remembered manual-slot marker.

There are ten numbered manual slots plus the separate autosave entry. Slot summaries vary by context: the in-game Save panel shows timestamp plus research, constructed-building, and inventory-key counts; main-menu and load cards expose their own compact progress fields. Loading replaces the active colony state, so confirm the target slot and timestamp before proceeding.
bullets: Autosave can be enabled or disabled, and its interval can be set from 1 to 30 minutes.
A manual save records current play time before writing, then starts a fresh in-session timer.
Guide unlocks, Guide read state, dismissed narrative messages, late-access archive state, boards, filters, automation history, and programs are part of save data.
General display, language, graphics, audio, and hotkey preferences are global application settings rather than colony progression.

sections.title: Storage safety
paragraphs: The game keeps local save records and, in the desktop build, can maintain an Electron-side mirror and backup copies. On startup it checks storage health and can attempt recovery from the mirror. A recovery notification is evidence that a fallback copy was used; save again once you have verified the colony state.

Export All creates one JSON archive containing the available primary saves, numbered slots, autosave, last-slot marker, shadow copies, and rotating local backups. Import Archive restores recognized save-storage records from that archive; it is broader than importing a single selected slot. Keep an export before moving between machines, testing development builds, or making a high-risk late-game change to a heavily automated colony.

media.alt: The Save Game overlay showing manual slots, autosave information, and storage safety controls.
media.caption: Manual slots and recovery tools.

sections.title: Compatibility and old saves
paragraphs: When a save predates a system, missing fields are initialized during loading. The game reconstructs reasonable defaults for research filters, Almanac options, operations boards, automation state, archive records, and Guide state. Existing progress is not supposed to be discarded merely because a later build added a new interface.

callout.title: A save is not a screenshot
callout.body: If you need to report a progression defect, export the affected slot before trying corrective actions. A picture shows the symptom; the save preserves the exact industrial state that produced it.

sections.title: Save and load confirmations
bullets: Saving into an occupied numbered slot asks for overwrite confirmation. Saving into an empty slot does not.

Loading an existing slot asks for confirmation because unsaved current progress will be lost. Import Archive itself writes recognized archive records without an overwrite confirmation; the later prompt controls whether its restored primary save is loaded into the active session, not whether storage has already been replaced.
The in-game Save panel lists all ten manual slots, including empty ones. The Load panel lists only existing autosave and manual records.
Returning to Main Menu is not itself a save action. Save first, then confirm the return.

buildings-directory.title: Buildings Directory
buildings-directory.summary: Locked, constructible, and operational facilities; filtering, sorting, and quick selection.

sections.title: Three building states
paragraphs: Researching a building never pays its construction cost. Constructing consumes the listed resources once and permanently adds that facility type to the colony. A recipe can be researched while its assigned building remains unconstructed; in that case the recipe is known but cannot be run.
bullets: Locked: the required research has not been completed. The reverse side of the card can lead to the relevant research node.
Unlocked, not constructed: the design is known, but the facility is not operational. Its card shows construction requirements and offers the Construct Building action.
Operational: the building has been constructed. Select the card to open its production interface.

media.alt: The Buildings directory with one locked card, one constructible card shown from the back, and one operational card.
media.caption: Read a facility card by its state before opening it.

sections.title: Finding the right facility
bullets: Search ranks matches from the displayed building name first, then internal identifier and description. It immediately narrows the grid.

The four category filters are All, Gathering, Production, and Power. Production is the broad group: it includes smelting, crafting, processing, manufacturing, chemical, electronics, and research facilities.
Unlocked Only removes designs that cannot yet be built or opened.
Sort by Technology Level to follow progression, or alphabetically when you already know the facility name.
Arrow-key navigation and search suggestions allow fast keyboard opening. Use Enter to open the highlighted building.

sections.title: Card interactions
paragraphs: Hovering a locked or constructible card exposes its reverse-side information. Resource requirements are interactive: hover for identity and inventory information, click to open that resource in the Almanac, or pin the complete construction requirement to the Operations Board.
A remembered Buildings-list position is useful in a large catalogue. If enabled in Settings, returning from production can restore your previous location rather than forcing the directory to the top.

building-construction.title: Building Construction
building-construction.summary: Permanent facilities, construction costs, unmet requirements, and board tracking.
building-construction.unlockLabel: Unlocked when your first additional building design becomes available

sections.title: Research, then provision, then construct
steps: Complete the technology that unlocks the building design.
Find the building in the Buildings directory. Its state changes from locked to construction-ready.
Inspect every required material on the back of the card. Red or insufficient amounts must be produced first.
Optionally pin the requirements to the Operations Board so totals stay visible while you visit other screens.
Press Construct Building. The complete cost is removed atomically; partial construction is not stored.
Open the now-operational card and select one of the recipes you have researched for it.

media.alt: A construction-ready building card with resource costs, insufficient amounts, Almanac links, and the pin control.
media.caption: Construction requirements are separate from recipe inputs.

sections.title: Specific rules
bullets: Construction is permanent within the save. Buildings are not sold, dismantled, or individually duplicated.
The Buildings counter in the header counts constructed facility types against the facility catalogue, including the two starting gathering sites.
If a contextual link opens production for an unconstructed building, the game redirects you to the Buildings directory and focuses the required facility.

Operations Board auto-react removes a pinned construction item after that building is successfully constructed. Disable auto-react if you want completed reference items to remain until manually removed.
Automation installation is a later, separate per-building cost. Constructing a facility does not include an automation core.

sections.title: Planning construction chains
paragraphs: A construction cost is best treated as a one-time project layered on top of ongoing recipe demand. If a material is also needed for immediate research, pin both targets and inspect the aggregated totals before spending it. The board deliberately shows the live inventory against the combined requirement so a “ready” construction does not conceal another shortage.

production-interface.title: Production Interface
production-interface.summary: Selecting recipes, reading the process diagram, producing, and moving between dependencies.
production-interface.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening a production building for the first time

sections.title: Screen anatomy
paragraphs: The recipe list contains only recipes unlocked for the current building. Search matches recipe name, recipe description, or the displayed name of an output resource; it does not search inputs. Selecting a card loads the complete process into the main panel: inputs, outputs, and separate tool or fuel requirements.

A building may have many possible processes but only one manually selected recipe at a time. The last selected recipe is stored per building, so returning to that facility normally restores your working context.

media.alt: A complete production screen with recipe list, selected recipe, process diagram, amount controls, fuel or tool requirements, and Produce button.
media.caption: All immediate costs should be visible before execution.

sections.title: Executing a manual batch
steps: Choose a recipe from the building list.

If the recipe offers fuel choices, inspect the selector. The first option is selected automatically whenever the recipe changes. Fuel is an additional cost and must not be confused with the normal input list.
Set the number of iterations with the stepper, a preset, or MAX.
Read the preview totals. They scale inputs, outputs, fuel, and tools to the selected amount.

Press Produce or use the Produce hotkey. The button is enabled only when the live combined requirement check succeeds. Outputs are added immediately after payment; manual production has no elapsed processing phase.

sections.title: Dependencies are interactive
paragraphs: Resource icons expose inventory and identity information. From supported resource interactions you can open the exact Almanac record, inspect where a resource is produced or consumed, and jump to another production building. Pinning the selected recipe creates a persistent project on the Operations Board, including the chosen iteration count and fuel.

The interface can be hidden with its view toggle or hotkey to reveal the facility background. This is purely visual; it does not start or interrupt production. Ambient audio and production music behavior are controlled separately in Settings.

production-batches-and-costs.title: Recipes, Batches, and Costs
production-batches-and-costs.summary: Iterations, scaled totals, MAX, profitability, and exact resource accounting.
production-batches-and-costs.unlockLabel: Unlocked with the Production Interface record

sections.title: An amount is a number of recipe iterations
paragraphs: If one iteration consumes 2 units and outputs 3, an amount of 10 consumes 20 and outputs 30. The amount field does not mean “desired output units” unless that recipe happens to output exactly one unit per iteration. Always read the scaled preview rather than inferring totals from the button label.

MAX computes the greatest batch currently supported by ordinary inputs, the selected fuel, tool capacity, and any recipe-specific cap. If no fuel is selected yet, the interface can evaluate available options to find a permissive maximum, but you must still confirm the actual fuel choice before producing.

sections.title: What counts as a cost
bullets: Inputs: consumed once per iteration according to the recipe map.
Fuel: consumed in addition to inputs, using the selected option and its per-iteration amount.
Tools: consumed in whole items according to durability capacity, rounded upward.
Construction materials: unrelated to a recipe batch; they are paid once when a facility is constructed.
Automation electricity: a time-based operating demand estimated and consumed by active electronic programs, not part of a manual Produce click.

callout.title: Manual tool payment is a separate transaction
callout.body: The current manual-production handler removes whole tools before it removes the ordinary input-and-fuel map. The button normally prevents an unaffordable attempt, but if inventory changes between those checks, a removed tool is not automatically restored when the later payment fails. Leave a buffer when automation is competing for the same stock.

sections.title: Profitability and industrial value
paragraphs: Recipe profitability is an informational ratio used by the Almanac’s recipe intelligence. It helps compare transformations but is not money, a guaranteed optimum, or a substitute for dependency planning. A lower-ratio process may be strategically essential because it unlocks a chain, uses a resource you have in abundance, or avoids a bottleneck elsewhere.

Inventory and production values can contain decimals for some processes. The interface formats values for readability, while the state keeps controlled precision. Do not plan around visual rounding at the edge of affordability; leave a small buffer for multi-stage chains.

callout.title: The Operations Board uses live totals
callout.body: For a pinned recipe, changing iterations or fuel on the board immediately recalculates requirements. This is safer than memorizing a preview from an earlier inventory state.

gathering-and-cooldowns.title: Gathering and Cooldowns
gathering-and-cooldowns.summary: Starting resources, finite manual batches, replenishment, and tool-assisted gathering.
gathering-and-cooldowns.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening any production building

sections.title: Starting extraction
paragraphs: Tree Grove and Stone Outcrop begin constructed and provide the hand-gathering recipes needed to start the colony. Hand gathering has no input resource, but it is still a recipe: select an amount, respect its maximum batch, produce, then wait for the site to replenish if that recipe has a cooldown.

Cooldowns are tracked by building and recipe in the save. Leaving the production screen does not reset them. When the timer expires, the interface and notification system can report that extraction is available again.

Automation does not write to this manual cooldown record. Instead, a recipe cooldown becomes a minimum duration for that automated Production block. Manual availability and automated cycle timing are therefore separate clocks.

sections.title: Maximum gathering
bullets: A displayed maximum batch is a hard per-operation limit for that recipe, even if your inventory could support a larger number.
For tool-assisted gathering, the maximum can also be constrained by how much work your tools can cover.
Pressing Produce while a cooldown remains does not consume inputs; it reports the remaining wait.
The MAX preset respects the current recipe cap and requirements. It is not an instruction to drain the entire colony inventory indiscriminately.

sections.title: When to stop gathering by hand
paragraphs: Hand gathering is reliable but slow. Tool recipes produce larger batches, and later mines or industrial extraction facilities shift the bottleneck away from repeated starter-site cooldowns. Nevertheless, early resources continue to feed construction, fuel, chemicals, and components, so “advanced” does not mean “safe to ignore.”

callout.title: Recorded activity
callout.body: Statistics distinguish gathering without tools, large single operations, total production, and output by building. These counters describe what happened; they do not alter cooldowns or recipe yields.

tools-and-efficiency.title: Tools and Efficiency
tools-and-efficiency.summary: Whole-tool consumption, durability as batch capacity, and avoiding wasted uses.

sections.title: Durability is capacity, not a health bar
paragraphs: Tools do not remain in inventory with partially depleted durability. A tool with durability 10 covers up to 10 recipe iterations in one production calculation. The game consumes the number of whole tools required: tools needed = ceiling(iterations ÷ durability).

That ceiling is the crucial detail. Producing 11 iterations with durability 10 consumes two tools, even though the second tool supplies only one useful iteration. The unused nine points of capacity are not stored for later.

media.alt: A tool requirement panel showing durability, selected batch, wasted capacity warning, and the Set to Optimal action.
media.caption: Match batches to whole durability multiples when resources permit.

sections.title: Efficient batch examples
paragraphs: When tool-efficiency warnings are enabled, a non-multiple batch shows its warning after a 500 ms delay so rapid stepper changes do not make the layout jump. Set to Optimal normally raises the amount to the full capacity of the whole tools already required; if that would exceed maxBatchSize, it falls back to a lower complete durability multiple when one exists. Disabling the warning hides this advice and does not change consumption.
bullets: Durability 10, amount 10: 1 tool, no unused capacity.
Durability 10, amount 11: 2 tools, 9 capacity wasted.
Durability 10, amount 20: 2 tools, no unused capacity.
Durability 10, amount 1: 1 tool is consumed; producing a tiny emergency batch can be valid, but it is intentionally inefficient.

sections.title: Tool progression
paragraphs: Better tool families generally support stronger gathering recipes and larger useful batches. They are manufactured resources with their own upstream costs, not permanent upgrades applied to the player. Keep spare tools before entering a mining or gathering phase, and include their production chain when estimating the true cost of extracted material.

callout.title: The preview is authoritative
callout.body: A recipe can require both ordinary inputs and a tool. The tool line is separate from the input diagram, but it is still consumed when the operation succeeds.

inventory-and-resources.title: Inventory and Resources
inventory-and-resources.summary: Live stock, actual resource flow, deficit filtering, and direct resource navigation.
inventory-and-resources.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening Inventory for the first time

sections.title: Read stock and flow together
paragraphs: Inventory is a colony-wide resource ledger. Every row shows the resource identity, current stored amount, actual automated inputs per minute, actual automated outputs per minute, and the resulting net flow. Descriptions remain in shared tooltips and the Almanac, keeping the table compact.

Rates use the same Actual calculation as the Automation Board. Running automation contributes to flow; blocked and inactive operations contribute zero. Electricity remains visible in the automation interfaces and is excluded from this resource table.

sections.title: Find pressure points
bullets: Negative Net/min is red and means the stock is shrinking; positive Net/min is green and means it is growing.
A deficit row estimates how long the current stock will last at the displayed rate.
Filter by All, Deficits, Surpluses, Active flow, or Zero stock, and search by displayed name or internal resource ID.
Select any column heading to sort. The chosen sort and flow filter are stored with the save.
Show discovered zero-stock resources restores dormant discovered resources to the full table.

sections.title: Move from signal to action
paragraphs: Left-click a row to open the resource in the Almanac. Hover for the standard resource tooltip, or right-click for the shared Where produced and Where used lookup with direct production navigation.
Inventory reports the resource situation. Scheme design, nominal rates, electricity, and production history remain in the automation interfaces.

resource-interactions.title: Resource Tooltips and Lookups
resource-interactions.summary: Hover summaries, context actions, live amounts, and dependency jumps.
resource-interactions.unlockLabel: Unlocked after inspecting a resource-oriented screen

sections.title: Hover for identity; interact for context
paragraphs: Resource tooltips are shared across production, research, construction, boards, and the Almanac. A normal hover can show the resource image, name, inventory amount, calculated value, and description. The live amount may continue changing while automation runs.

Interactive resource affordances can expose Where Produced and Where Used views. These are computed from recipe data rather than from your current stock. A listed recipe may be researched, unresearched, or assigned to an unconstructed building; status markings and action labels explain which jump is currently possible.

sections.title: Recipe lookup behavior
bullets: Where Produced lists recipes whose outputs contain the selected resource.

Where Used currently indexes only the ordinary recipe.inputs map. A resource used solely as a fuel option or solely as toolRequired will not appear there, even though the recipe card itself still displays its fuel and tool requirements.
Opening Production succeeds only for an unlocked recipe in a constructed building. Otherwise the game can lead to Research or the Buildings directory.
Clicking outside an interactive lookup closes it. Simple hover summaries do not capture clicks.
Recipe-preview tooltips can be disabled globally if detailed hover cards obscure the interface; direct Almanac and lookup navigation remains the durable source of information.

sections.title: Avoiding stale assumptions
paragraphs: A tooltip amount is a momentary inventory reading. For large plans, pin the recipe or construction project and use the Operations Board’s live aggregate. That board re-evaluates stock after every production or automation event, whereas a remembered tooltip does not.

fuel-and-electricity.title: Fuel, Electricity, and Power
fuel-and-electricity.summary: Fuel options, power as a stored resource, generation, and automation demand.

sections.title: Fuel is separate from recipe inputs
paragraphs: Some recipes expose several fuel options. Each option identifies a resource and a quantity consumed per iteration. Select one before production; the chosen fuel scales with the batch and is removed in addition to ordinary inputs.

Different fuels can make the same process practical at different stages. The interface does not automatically preserve an unavailable choice by secretly substituting another fuel. If the selected option is insufficient, choose another or produce more of it.

media.alt: A fuel selector with multiple fuel resources beside a power-generation recipe and the header electricity cell.
media.caption: Fuel choice and electricity stock are explicit resources.

sections.title: Electricity is inventory
paragraphs: Power-generation recipes output Electricity into the same colony inventory used by other resources. Manual recipes may consume electricity as a fuel or input. Active electronic automation consumes electricity over time according to its current program, building, batch, and speed configuration.
The header’s Electricity cell shows current stock, not generation rate. Generation rate and automation demand are different measurements; use the Automation Board to compare per-minute flow.
bullets: A power building must be researched, constructed, supplied, and operated like any other facility.

An electronic Production block without an error route waits and reports a blocked state when required electricity is unavailable. If its error port is connected, the failed attempt follows that route instead of waiting.
Speed upgrades increase throughput but multiply power demand. Purchased speed levels can be dialed down without refunding the upgrade.

On the Automation Board, Gross flow separates estimated automated outputs and inputs; Net flow subtracts opposing automated rates by resource. Manual Produce clicks have no continuous per-minute rate and are not part of those flow estimates.

sections.title: Fuel in plans and programs
paragraphs: A pinned recipe stores a board-specific fuel choice and includes it in Operations Board totals. An automation Production block also stores its own fuel choice. The manual selector is temporary and resets to the recipe’s first option when that recipe is selected again; changing it does not retroactively rewrite a pinned project or automation block.

research-tree.title: Research Tree
research-tree.summary: Availability, prerequisites, costs, node states, filters, and direct focus links.
research-tree.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening Research for the first time

sections.title: How a technology becomes available
paragraphs: A research node is available when every technology listed as its prerequisite is complete. Availability does not mean affordability: expand the node and compare its resource cost with live inventory. Completing research consumes those resources, then permanently records the technology in the save.

Research can unlock one or more recipes, a building design, or a supporting technology used only as a prerequisite. A recipe unlock and a building unlock are independent. When both are granted together, the new facility still requires construction before production can occur.

media.alt: The Research Tree showing researched, available, and locked nodes across tier backgrounds, with a node detail panel open.
media.caption: Follow prerequisite edges, then inspect the resource cost.

sections.title: Node states and graph reading
bullets: Researched nodes are complete. Select one to review what it unlocked.
Available nodes have all prerequisites complete. Select one to inspect cost and perform the research.
Locked nodes still have prerequisite work. Hover to emphasize the relevant past and future graph connections.
Tier backgrounds group technologies by broad complexity, but visible edges—not horizontal position alone—define prerequisites.
The legend reports current state colors. Do not infer availability from a technology’s name or tier number.

sections.title: Navigation and filtering
bullets: Research search opens up to eight ranked suggestions; it does not remove nonmatching nodes from the graph. It matches research name or description, names of buildings unlocked by that research, and names of recipes it unlocks. Arrow keys move through suggestions, Enter focuses the highlighted node, and Escape clears the query.
Contextual Open Research actions from another system focus the exact technology node even in a large tree.
Tier toggles can hide entire tiers without changing progress.
Show only researched & available removes locked nodes for a cleaner working view.
Tier navigation jumps the camera directly to a chosen tier.
Zoom, fit-view, and interaction-lock controls affect only the graph viewport.
Your visible tiers, availability filter, and viewport are saved per colony.

callout.title: Pin expensive research
callout.body: Pinning a research node adds its complete cost to the Operations Board. With auto-react enabled, the item is removed after the technology is completed.

research-progression.title: Technology Tiers and Progression
research-progression.summary: Highest-tier tracking, cross-tier dependencies, new music, and strategic research order.
research-progression.unlockLabel: Unlocked after completing your first research project

sections.title: Highest Technology Tier
paragraphs: The header displays the highest technology tier you have reached, defined by the highest-tier completed research. It is not an average and does not require every lower-tier node to be complete. Reaching a tier can expand colony capacity and unlock that tier’s soundtrack, but individual recipes and buildings still follow their own research prerequisites.

Some branches reconnect after several tiers. If a seemingly modest material blocks advanced work, trace the required-research edges and use the Almanac to identify its production route instead of assuming that every prerequisite must be located in the same visible tier.

sections.title: What changes when a new tier is reached
bullets: The highest-tier status cell updates.
The music manager unlocks tracks assigned to that tier. The Jukebox can then enable or disable individual unlocked tracks.
Colonist capacity rises with tier progression. Capacity and active reservations are visible in the header.
At later thresholds, additional systems may become accessible. The exact triggering technology or interface event still controls its Guide record.
The accumulated play-time timestamp of each newly reached highest tier is recorded for the Statistics progression chart; it does not impose a time limit.

sections.title: Choosing research intelligently
paragraphs: Prioritize the bottleneck, not merely the numerically highest available node. A new mine can solve raw-material pressure; a processing method can multiply the usefulness of existing ore; a power branch can support future automation; a construction-enabling intermediate may unblock several facilities at once.

Before paying a large research cost, inspect its unlock list and the construction costs of any new building. Research without the materials to build or feed its facility is still valid progress, but it may not solve your immediate production problem.

callout.title: A faint administrative irregularity
callout.body: Tier timestamps are preserved with more care than some personnel records. This has no effect on the research graph. It is, apparently, excellent paperwork.

almanac-basics.title: Resource Almanac
almanac-basics.summary: The book, contents, alphabetical navigation, options, and resource records.
almanac-basics.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening the Almanac for the first time

sections.title: A complete resource catalogue
paragraphs: The Almanac contains every resource record in the active game data, including materials not yet present in inventory. A resource page can include its category, image, material value, description, chemical formula, historical background, and factual notes. The book is therefore both a production reference and the game’s industrial encyclopedia.

Opening the Almanac from a resource interaction focuses that exact resource. Opening it from the navigation tab uses the configured starting page: cover by default, or Table of Contents if Open on contents page is enabled.

media.alt: An Almanac spread showing a resource page, page navigation, options, and the View Recipes control.
media.caption: Resource identity and production context share one record.

sections.title: Finding a page
bullets: The current Almanac has no free-text resource search. Use the Table of Contents, its alphabet jump controls, or a contextual resource link from Inventory, Production, Research, construction, or a board.
Selecting a Table of Contents row jumps directly to that resource page.
Alphabet buttons scroll the Table of Contents to a starting-letter group; they do not remove other rows. These buttons are omitted in the Chinese locale, where Latin initial grouping is not used.
Cover, Contents, Previous, and Next controls provide deterministic navigation even when realistic page flipping is disabled.
Clicking the resource image opens a larger image view.
Page-flip activity is tracked for Statistics and achievements; it does not unlock recipes.

sections.title: Almanac options
bullets: Open on contents page changes where ordinary Almanac visits begin.
Hide unresearched recipes removes recipes you have not unlocked from recipe lookup.
Hide recipes for unbuilt buildings removes processes assigned to facilities you have not constructed.
These filters simplify the visible lookup; they do not delete recipe knowledge or change the production graph.
Realistic page flipping is a global interface setting. Dragging page edges is optional; navigation buttons remain available.

sections.title: Material value is not currency
paragraphs: Material Value is precomputed from the complete recipe data, not from the recipes researched in this save. No-input outputs and Electricity begin at a base value of 1. Other values propagate through input and fuel costs per unit of output, keep the lowest calculable route, and never fall below 1; an unresolved resource also falls back to 1. Tool cost is not part of that value calculation. The number is useful for broad comparison, but the colony has no market and cannot sell a resource for it.

almanac-recipe-intelligence.title: Almanac Recipe Intelligence
almanac-recipe-intelligence.summary: Producing and consuming recipes, status markings, profitability, and contextual jumps.
almanac-recipe-intelligence.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening View Recipes in the Almanac

sections.title: Two directions through the graph
paragraphs: View Recipes opens a panel divided into Producing Recipes and Consuming Recipes. Producing recipes have the current resource in outputs. Consuming recipes have it in ordinary inputs. Fuel-only and tool-only relationships are not indexed as consumers in the current implementation, so inspect recipe cards when planning those special costs.

Each recipe card exposes its assigned building, input and output maps, fuel or tool information where applicable, profitability, and research / construction status. The current resource is highlighted inside the card so it remains clear which side of the transformation you are inspecting.

media.alt: The Almanac Recipe Lookup with producing and consuming cards in researched, unresearched, and unbuilt-building states.
media.caption: Status-aware links turn the catalogue into a navigation hub.

sections.title: Action changes by status
bullets: Researched recipe + constructed building: View in Production opens the correct building and selects the recipe.
Researched recipe + unconstructed building: Open in Buildings focuses the facility you must construct.
Unresearched recipe: Open Required Research focuses the technology that unlocks it.
Striped or labeled cards indicate unavailable knowledge rather than missing data.

Can be produced now is a one-iteration affordability hint. It checks recipe research, ordinary inputs, at least one valid fuel option, and at least one required tool. It does not check whether the assigned building is constructed, does not test a manual cooldown, and does not promise that your selected multi-iteration batch is affordable.

sections.title: Using profitability without being misled
paragraphs: Profitability is a stored ratio derived from calculated output value divided by calculated input cost. Its calculation can include proportional tool value and fuel cost, but that theoretical accounting is not the same as the whole-tool ceiling applied to an actual batch. Construction, research, cooldown opportunity, fuel availability, and automation power can still change the practical answer.

The most profitable theoretical recipe may belong to an unbuilt facility or require an unavailable branch. Use the Almanac options to hide such routes when you need an immediately actionable plan, then disable the filters when planning ahead.

operations-board.title: Operations Board
operations-board.summary: Pinned tasks, target projects, blueprint timers, aggregate requirements, fuel choices, and auto-react.
operations-board.unlockLabel: Unlocked after pinning your first recipe, research, or construction project

sections.title: A cross-screen project list
paragraphs: The Operations Board tracks recipes, research costs, and building-construction costs in one persistent panel. Pin controls appear in those systems. Open or collapse the board with its edge handle or hotkey; collapsing does not remove its items.

At the top, Total Requirements aggregates every pinned item. Each resource compares the combined requirement with live inventory, so producing a material can turn a shortage into a satisfied row without reopening the board.

media.alt: The expanded Operations Board with aggregate resource chips and pinned recipe, research, and building items.
media.caption: One live plan can span the entire colony.

sections.title: Item-specific behavior
bullets: Recipe items allow the iteration count to be increased or decreased. Inputs, outputs, fuel, and tool demand recalculate immediately.
Recipes with fuel options preserve a board-specific selected fuel.
Research items show the exact cost and jump back to the focused research node.
Building items show construction requirements and jump to the focused building card.
A recipe whose facility is not constructed reports that blocker and can redirect you to Buildings.
Unpin removes only that project. Clear All removes every project immediately and does not ask for confirmation. Neither action consumes nor refunds resources.

sections.title: Auto-react to game events
paragraphs: With Auto-react enabled, a pinned research item is removed when that research completes, a construction item is removed when its building is constructed, and a recipe item counts down after matching manual or automated iterations complete. The manual-production path shows a throttled progress or removal notification. Automation applies the same countdown inside its simulation tick but does not emit that board-specific toast, so an automated target can decrease or disappear quietly.
With Auto-react disabled, the board becomes a static reference list. This is useful for recurring production targets or when you want a completed project to remain as a template.

callout.title: The board is a calculator, not a reservation system
callout.body: Pinned requirements do not lock inventory. You can spend those resources elsewhere, and the live status will return to insufficient. The board never executes production or research on its own.

sections.title: Creating a project
paragraphs: New Project selects a target resource and amount, an unbuilt building, or an unfinished research target. A resource amount is treated as a new output batch: the project can be created even if that resource already exists in inventory, while current stock is used as starter stock for inputs and intermediates.

Project settings are saved with the board. Use only researched recipes restricts the chain to recipes currently researched; disabling it lets the planner use all recipe data. Prefer highest-efficiency recipes chooses the best allowed recipe by efficiency value. The resource blacklist rejects any recipe whose inputs, tools, or fuel include a blocked resource.
If the planner cannot fully resolve the chain with the current settings, the dialog shows a warning and no project cards are pinned.
bullets: Resource selectors show icons and resource tooltips.
The building selector lists only unbuilt buildings.
The research selector lists only unfinished research.
Blueprint project buttons on building cards and research nodes start a project for that target; pressing the same button again removes that project.
The help button in the project dialog opens this Guide record.

sections.title: Development timer and project cards
paragraphs: A newly created project appears as a collapsed locked blueprint node. It shows the final target and development timer, but its step count and total requirements are hidden until development completes.
When the timer ends, the planner rebuilds the final chain from the inventory state at that moment. Resources produced during development can reduce or change the completed project plan.

A ready project expands on the board and sends a blueprint-style notification. Its cards are grouped, numbered in execution order, and the final card is marked; project cards cannot be unpinned one by one, so use the group header to remove the whole project.
bullets: A collapsed ready project occupies board space as one node and shows the final step.

Series guidance appears only when a recipe uses returned resources and the full amount cannot be produced as one affordable batch. Open Next Batch starts the currently affordable batch; if the full batch is already affordable, the Series label is hidden.

callout.title: Development time
callout.body: Time = resolved steps × 5 seconds × tier coefficient. The coefficient is 1 at tier 1 and rises linearly to 5 at tier 10: 1 + (tier - 1) × 4 / 9. Resource projects use the tech level of the final recipe building; building projects use the target building tier; research projects use the research tier.

colony-status-deck.title: Colony Status Deck
colony-status-deck.summary: Total output, facilities, tier, colonists, active schemes, blockers, and electricity.

sections.title: Colony progress bank
paragraphs: These values summarize progression; they are not buttons. Detailed breakdowns live in Statistics, Buildings, and Research.
bullets: Total Production is the cumulative number of output units produced, not current inventory. Consumption does not subtract from it.
Buildings shows constructed facility types against the valid building catalogue.
Tier shows the highest completed research tier.

media.alt: The full status deck with progress and operations banks annotated by metric.
media.caption: Current stock, cumulative output, and capacity are different measurements.

sections.title: Colony operations bank
paragraphs: A blocked scheme remains active but cannot advance its current work. Open its building or the Automation Board to identify missing resources or electricity. A stopped scheme is not counted as active and does not reserve colonists.
bullets: Colonists shows available / total. The detail line reports how many are reserved by running manual automation programs.
Active Schemes counts running manual and electronic programs. If any has a blocked reason, the cell reports the number blocked.
Electricity shows current inventory, not per-minute generation or consumption.

sections.title: The central mark
paragraphs: The central Realindustry wordmark is a permanent part of the header. Some late interface sequences may attach meaning or interaction to that mark. If the interface begins behaving as though a decorative element has acquired administrative significance, this Guide recommends professional curiosity and a backup save.

achievements.title: Achievements and Rewards
achievements.summary: Categories, rarity, progress, hidden goals, awarding organizations, and achievement reward bonuses.
achievements.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening Achievements for the first time

sections.title: What an achievement records
paragraphs: Achievements evaluate saved colony statistics and event counters: production totals, specific resources, research, construction, interface use, time patterns, automation, and other milestones. Unlocking an achievement records its identifier permanently in the save and displays an award notification.

The Achievements overlay can be filtered by category and searched. Each card identifies rarity, progress where the condition exposes a measurable target, reward text, and the awarding organization. Locked artwork may be concealed until earned.

media.alt: The Achievements overlay with category filters, progress bars, rarity styling, and one unlocked award.
media.caption: Achievements record colony history and can grant practical bonuses in the current save.

sections.title: Practical rewards
paragraphs: Achievements can grant practical rewards in the current save: one-time resource grants, future cost reductions, or output bonuses for matching resources, buildings, recipe technology levels, production modes, or the whole colony.

Active bonuses are calculated from unlocked achievements and current reward definitions. Balance changes in later patches therefore update the bonus values instead of storing old numbers permanently in the save.
bullets: Output bonuses affect only newly produced recipe output. Returned input amounts, fuel, electricity, tools, and automation overhead are not multiplied.
Some bonuses have narrow scopes, such as recipes known at the moment the achievement was earned, manual production only, or currently active automation only.

sections.title: Output rounding
paragraphs: Produced output is calculated from the recipe's base output, the number of batch or automation iterations, and every eligible achievement bonus.
Recipes that normally produce whole units discard any fractional remainder after bonuses. A small bonus may do nothing on a single craft, but becomes useful when the batch is large enough.
Recipes whose base output is already fractional keep decimal output.

callout.title: Output tooltip
callout.body: Production and Almanac output numbers already show the real produced amount. Hover them to see the base amount, the amount after bonuses, the final produced amount, and the achievements that affected it.

sections.title: Important limitations
bullets: Not every condition reveals its exact target before completion.
Progress can update after the relevant production, research, construction, Almanac, menu, or activity counter changes.
An achievement notification does not imply that a recipe, building, or protected archive entry was unlocked unless that system separately says so.
Statistics can help diagnose measurable goals, but hidden or behavioral achievements may require experimentation.

sections.title: Corporate awards language
paragraphs: Award notes are written from the perspective of several organizations, including internal corporate bodies. Their tone is part of the setting. “Performance within expected parameters” is still an achievement, even if whoever wrote it appears constitutionally unable to sound pleased.

statistics-dashboard.title: Statistics Dashboard
statistics-dashboard.summary: Overview, production, activity, tier timing, and automation accounting.
statistics-dashboard.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening Statistics for the first time

sections.title: Overview tab
paragraphs: Overview summarizes resource keys present in the inventory object, constructed buildings, completed research, total play time, total production, production per hour, the ten largest current stockpiles, technology-tier progression, and automated output. The “unique resources” card counts stored inventory keys, including a key whose amount has later reached zero; it is not necessarily the number of visible positive-amount Inventory cards. Production per hour uses accumulated play time, so it is a long-run historical rate rather than an instantaneous machine rate.

media.alt: Statistics Overview with summary cards, top resources, and technology tier progression.
media.caption: Use the dashboard to understand history, not to control production.

sections.title: Production tab
bullets: Top Produced Resources is cumulative output by resource, not current stock.
Production by Building attributes manual and tracked output to facility types.
Largest Output in One Operation records the largest completed output event. Both manual production and automated Production blocks can raise it.
Gathering Without Tools tracks the early extraction behavior separately.

Total Recycled is updated only by recycling-category buildings. Manual recycling counts ordinary inputs and fuel; separately removed tools are not included. Automated recycling counts every physical requirement, including tools and fuel, but excludes automation Electricity.

Automation counters include output, physical input consumption, electricity consumption, completed Production-block cycles, and configured recipe iterations. One completed block raises cycles by 1 and iterations by that block’s batch count.

sections.title: Activity tab
bullets: Most Used Features is based on tracked button and navigation interactions.
Almanac flips, menu opens, days played, and music tracks heard are historical counters.
Days played uses distinct calendar dates encountered by the save, not total play time divided by 24 hours.
Tracks heard are synchronized from the music manager before opening Statistics so the count reflects the current session.

callout.title: A number can be true in two different ways
callout.body: Inventory answers “How much exists now?” Statistics answers “How much has happened?” The distinction matters whenever a resource is produced and immediately consumed upstream.

notifications-and-idle.title: Notifications and Idle Monitoring
notifications-and-idle.summary: Message types, board updates, cooldown notices, and the inactivity protocol.
notifications-and-idle.unlockLabel: Unlocked after completing your first research project

sections.title: Notification types
paragraphs: A notification is transient; the underlying state is not. If a message disappears, inspect the relevant screen, Guide record, or saved dashboard rather than attempting to reproduce the action merely to read it again.
bullets: Success messages confirm completed actions such as saving, construction, automation installation, or production.
Information messages explain state changes, cooldown completion, unlocks, and non-fatal blockers.
Error messages report missing resources, invalid programs, unavailable facilities, or storage problems.
Achievement and board notifications have dedicated styling and can summarize automatic project progress.
The live notification list keeps at most 24 items. If a burst exceeds that bound, the oldest active items are dropped and the newest are retained.

Most messages remove themselves after their configured duration. A persistent message remains until application logic removes or clears it; the current toast renderer has no user-operated close button.

sections.title: Idle monitoring
paragraphs: At 60 seconds without keyboard, pointer, wheel, scroll, touch, or click activity, the game displays an inactivity warning without sound. At 300 seconds it changes to a severe corporate warning and plays the warning sound. Any monitored interaction clears the warning and resets both thresholds.

Idle monitoring is presentation and lore. It does not delete resources, fail research, or impose a hidden production penalty. Automation may continue according to its own resource and electricity rules while the application remains active.

callout.title: Efficiency protocol
callout.body: The system’s concern about an unattended Director is operationally sincere and emotionally unhelpful. You may take breaks. No Guide record authorizes the colony to object.

settings-and-accessibility.title: Settings and Accessibility
settings-and-accessibility.summary: General behavior, display, graphics, audio, languages, and safe resets.
settings-and-accessibility.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening the in-game Menu for the first time

sections.title: General and interface settings
bullets: Language can follow the system or use a manually selected supported locale.
Autosave and its interval control the dedicated autosave record.

Notifications can be disabled for success, information, achievement, board, and similar messages sent through the notification provider. Error notifications deliberately bypass this preference. The separate idle-warning overlay is not controlled by this checkbox and still appears at its inactivity thresholds.
Recipe preview tooltips, hotkey hint badges, remembered Buildings position, and tool-efficiency warnings can be toggled independently.
Realistic Almanac page flipping is optional and does not remove button navigation.

sections.title: The in-game Menu shell
paragraphs: Menu contains Resume, Save Game, Load Game, Settings, Jukebox, Main Menu, and Exit. Clicking the dark area outside the menu behaves like Resume. Jukebox also shows the currently reported track beneath its button.

Main Menu and Exit require confirmation. In the Electron build, confirmed Exit asks the desktop shell to quit; in another host it uses the application’s fallback exit action. Opening and closing Menu does not pause, save, or roll back automation by itself.

sections.title: Display and graphics
paragraphs: Windowed, borderless where supported, and fullscreen modes control the shell. Windowed mode can use a chosen resolution. UI scale ranges from a compact to an enlarged interface, and building-grid scale changes how many facility cards fit in the directory.

Graphics quality and feature switches control shaders, WebGL effects, optical effects, realistic ambient particles, ordinary particle effects, animations, and the especially demanding Research Tree effects. Some controls depend on shaders, WebGL, or High quality and are disabled when those prerequisites are off.

media.alt: Settings with General, Display, Graphics, Audio, and Hotkeys tabs visible.
media.caption: Presentation can be reduced without changing simulation rules.

sections.title: Audio and safe use
bullets: Master, music, ambient, UI / sound-effect, and voice volumes are independent. Master scales every other channel.
Production music can be disabled for facility interfaces, left at normal level, or enabled with ducking. The ducking checkbox has no effect while Production Music itself is off.
Building ambient preview on card hover can be disabled.
The in-game music is original and intended to be safe for recorded videos and streams.
Reset restores setting defaults after confirmation. It is not the same action as resetting a save slot.

jukebox-and-audio.title: Jukebox and Dynamic Music
jukebox-and-audio.summary: Tier-based track unlocks, disabling tracks, production behavior, and heard-track statistics.
jukebox-and-audio.unlockLabel: Unlocked with the in-game Menu record

sections.title: Technology unlocks the soundtrack
paragraphs: Music is grouped by technology tier. Reaching a new highest tier unlocks its associated tracks in the active music manager. The Jukebox lists available tracks and can disable individual songs without lowering overall music volume.
Disabled tracks remain unlocked and can be restored later. A save keeps its disabled-track list, while general volume settings are application preferences.

sections.title: Music in production
bullets: Production Music determines whether the soundtrack continues while a facility interface is open.
Ducking reduces music volume substantially in production rather than stopping playback.
Ambient machinery and UI effects use separate volume channels.
Assistant transmissions and other voiced material use the voice channel.
Statistics records distinct tracks heard. It is not the same count as tracks unlocked or enabled.

sections.title: Missing a newly unlocked track
paragraphs: Check the Jukebox’s enabled state, music volume, master volume, and whether production music is disabled. Track selection remains dynamic; unlocking a tier expands the pool but does not guarantee that one exact track plays immediately.

automation-foundations.title: Automation Foundations
automation-foundations.summary: Building-local schemes, manual crews, later electronic cores, and operating modes.
automation-foundations.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening your first production interface

sections.title: Automation is local to each building
paragraphs: Automation means a saved executable scheme for one constructed facility. A building can hold a manual scheme from the beginning, and later can also hold an electronic scheme, core installation, upgrades, runtime tasks, selected mode, and history contribution. A program configured in one building cannot run a recipe assigned to another building.

Automation repeats recipe work over time instead of executing instantly. Physical inputs, selected fuel, and whole tools are removed when a Production block completes. Electronic Production blocks also remove their calculated Electricity. Outputs enter the same live inventory used by manual production and every other program.

media.alt: A production building’s automation console showing electronic and manual modes, core installation, program controls, and upgrades.
media.caption: Automation belongs to the facility whose recipes it executes.

sections.title: Two modes, one building
bullets: Colonist Automation is available through the manual scheme controls in a production building. It does not require Building Automation research or an installed electronic core.

Electronic Automation is the later core-based layer unlocked by Building Automation research. It requires an installed automation core in that building and consumes electricity while Production blocks operate.
A building cannot run its electronic and manual program simultaneously. Stop the active mode before starting the other.
Programs remain saved while stopped. Stopping clears active runtime tasks and reservations but does not delete the graph.
Ordinary manual Produce remains a separate action. A running program does not prevent you from viewing the production interface, but competing for the same inventory can create blockers.

sections.title: Installing an electronic core
steps: Research Building Automation.
Open an operational building and locate its automation console.
Inspect the building-specific installation cost.
Install Automation Core. The complete cost is consumed once for that building.
Configure and validate an Electronic scheme before starting it.

callout.title: Construction is not installation
callout.body: Building the facility, researching automation, and installing its core are three separate gates. An installed core also does not make an empty or invalid program run.

sections.title: Exact core installation cost
paragraphs: Let t be the building Technology Level clamped from 0 through 10. Installing that building’s electronic core costs the following whole units: Copper Wire = ceiling(30 + t³), Steel Gear = ceiling(5 + t²), Steel Plate = ceiling(4 + t^1.8), Electronic Circuit = ceiling(2 + t^1.5), and Motor = ceiling(2 + t^1.5). The formula is evaluated separately for every building; installing one core does not discount the next.

automation-program-editor.title: Automation Program Editor
automation-program-editor.summary: Creating graphs, connecting ports, checking, autosaving, clipboard actions, and starting schemes.
automation-program-editor.unlockLabel: Unlocked after opening a manual or electronic scheme editor

sections.title: A scheme is an executable graph
paragraphs: Drag a block to the canvas or click it in the palette, configure its fields, and connect output ports to compatible input ports. Execution begins at the single Start block and follows connections. Position is visual; connections and block data define behavior.

Changes are saved automatically to the building and mode. Connections, recipes, iteration counts, and other executable settings require Check Scheme again before launch. A Production block’s own power button is an operational control: switching it is saved immediately and does not invalidate an already checked graph. Check Scheme validates structure and highlights involved nodes or edges; Start Scheme is enabled only when launch requirements are satisfied.

media.alt: The automation editor with block palette, connected graph, minimap or controls, validation panel, and start lever.
media.caption: Connections, not screen position, define control flow.

sections.title: Editor controls
bullets: Ctrl + drag performs area selection.
Ctrl+A selects all. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V, and Ctrl+D copy, cut, paste, and duplicate selected fragments.
Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes.
Delete removes selected blocks or edges. Escape clears selection.
Double-click a connection to insert a reroute point; right-click a connection to remove it.
Snap to grid changes placement assistance only.
Clear removes the editable scheme after the relevant interaction; copy a reusable graph first if needed.

sections.title: Templates: a working structure to adapt
paragraphs: Open the Templates tab in the left palette to replace the current graph with a complete, prewired scheme. Templates are editable starting points, not locked programs: after insertion, you can move, reconnect, add, or delete any block. Applying one is a single undoable action, so Ctrl+Z restores the previous graph.

Production blocks initially use the current building’s first available recipe and its first compatible fuel choice. Before launch, review the recipe, fuel, and iteration count in every Production block, as well as the resource and threshold in every Condition block. A template is neither checked nor started automatically: adapt it first, then run Check Scheme.
bullets: The Standard scheme, marked Recommended, is the fastest starting point for one repeating production task. For the tutorial step, apply it and set the Production block to 10 iterations.
The Sequential scheme chains four Production blocks in one repeating route. All four initially use the same recipe, so configure each block for the sequence you actually need.
The Parallel scheme splits control into four independent repeating branches. Use it when several production tasks should progress side by side rather than wait for one another.

Electronic automation also offers Standard Conditional, Complex Sequential, Complex Conditional, and Parallel Conditional schemes. These provide ready-made structures for conditions, splits, joins, barriers, waits, and multiple loops.
Manual templates already include Rest blocks. Keep enough rest on every repeating route to satisfy colonist recovery requirements.

Some advanced electronic templates contain four Production blocks and require enough unlocked production slots. If validation reports a slot limit, simplify the graph or purchase more Parallel Controller levels.

sections.title: Copying between buildings and modes
paragraphs: Copy Scheme stores the complete graph in a persistent local scheme clipboard. Paste Scheme replaces the target editor’s entire graph; it is not an append operation. Unsupported block types are omitted for the target mode, electronic Production blocks beyond the current slot limit are omitted, manual error edges are removed, iteration counts are clamped, and a Production block whose saved recipe does not belong to the target building falls back to that building’s first available recipe and first fuel choice.

Selection copy/paste is separate. It stores selected blocks plus only the edges whose two endpoints are selected, then appends a new fragment near the camera center. Pasted blocks receive new identifiers. If the target electronic program lacks free Production slots, excess selected Production blocks and their now-invalid edges are skipped while other accepted blocks can still be pasted.
A copied graph is a design, not live runtime state. Progress, blocked resources, barrier arrivals, and current tasks are not a portable production queue.

callout.title: Build one valid pass before a repeating graph
callout.body: Start → Production → End is the smallest one-pass scheme. For a finite repeating scheme, use Start → Joiner → Production → Loop; connect Loop.body back to Joiner and Loop.exit to End. A manual version must place its required Rest block(s) on the repeating route, normally between Production and Loop. Start has no input port, and two routes cannot share one ordinary input port—this is why the Joiner is necessary.

automation-blocks.title: Automation Blocks and Flow
automation-blocks.summary: Every block type, port semantics, branching, synchronization, loops, errors, and reroutes.
